description: Refactor the SLA escalation worker from a standalone cron-script into an in-process setInterval worker wired into server.js. This feature is independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 — it only touches backend files.
steps: Edit backend/workers/slaEscalation.js: (a) Remove the `require('dotenv').config();` line at the top — dotenv is already loaded by server.js. (b) Remove `await mongoose.connect(process.env.MONGODB_URI);` and `console.log('[SLA Worker] Connected to MongoDB');` from checkSLABreaches(). (c) Remove the entire `finally { await mongoose.disconnect(); console.log('[SLA Worker] Disconnected from MongoDB'); }` block from checkSLABreaches() — replace it with a plain finally that only logs completion or keeps the error log. (d) Add a new exported function at the bottom of the file: `function startSlaWorker() { console.log('[SLA Worker] Starting in-process SLA escalation worker (15 min interval)'); checkSLABreaches(); const id = setInterval(checkSLABreaches, 15 * 60 * 1000); return id; }`. (e) Update the module.exports line to: `module.exports = { checkSLABreaches, startSlaWorker };`. (f) Keep the `if (require.main === module)` block as-is at the bottom so the script can still be run standalone for manual checks — but when run standalone, restore the mongoose.connect/disconnect inside that block only (i.e., call `mongoose.connect(process.env.MONGODB_URI)` before `checkSLABreaches()` and `mongoose.disconnect()` after, scoped to the `require.main` block).

Edit backend/server.js: (a) Add at the top with other requires: `const { startSlaWorker } = require('./workers/slaEscalation');`. (b) Inside the `start()` async function, after `app.listen(PORT, () => { console.log(...); });`, add `startSlaWorker();` on the next line, still inside the try block.
acceptance_criteria: The `checkSLABreaches` function no longer calls mongoose.connect() or mongoose.disconnect() in its main body.
`startSlaWorker()` calls checkSLABreaches() once immediately, then sets a 15-minute interval.
backend/server.js imports startSlaWorker and calls it after app.listen() in the start() function.
`node --check backend/workers/slaEscalation.js` passes with no syntax errors.
`node --check backend/server.js` passes with no syntax errors.
verification: Run `node --check backend/workers/slaEscalation.js` — must exit 0 with no output.
Run `node --check backend/server.js` — must exit 0 with no output.

Start the backend: `cd backend && node server.js` — confirm logs show '[SLA Worker] Starting in-process SLA escalation worker (15 min interval)' after 'API listening on port ...', with no 'mongoose.connect' errors.
findings: Implemented as specified. Removed top-level dotenv.config() and mongoose.connect/disconnect from checkSLABreaches(). Added startSlaWorker() that runs checkSLABreaches() immediately then on a 15-min setInterval. The require.main block uses the mongoose.connect().then(checkSLABreaches).then(mongoose.disconnect) promise chain for standalone use. server.js imports and calls startSlaWorker() after app.listen(). Both files pass node --check syntax verification.
